introH2: What kind of hotels does Kaset-Nawamin have — and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: Kaset-Nawamin is not a tourist district, but for travellers with real reasons to be here — parents visiting students at Kasetsart University Bangkhen, business travellers working the Ngamwongwan corridor, patients at Paolo Hospital Kaset, or anyone who wants a budget-friendly base on the northern BTS Green Line — this district has far more solid options than most people expect. The area includes Kasetsart University Bangkhen, BTS Green Line stations at Kasetsart University, Sena Nikhom and Ratchayothin, the Kaset Junction intersection, Ngamwongwan Road, Or Tor Kor Market, Big C Kaset, Paolo Hospital Kaset, and a dense network of student-priced food stalls. This article covers 7 hotels we have reviewed in detail — each with verified guest scores, honest pros and cons, and prices compared across Agoda, Trip.com and Booking.com.
mrtHtml: Three BTS Green Line stations serve this district: Ratchayothin (Metro Hotel 400 m walk, Pannapat Place 600 m walk) · Kasetsart University (Livotel Kaset 900 m, Maruay Garden 5-minute walk) · Sena Nikhom (P24 at Kaset 400 m walk) · Missoniya Hotel sits on Ngamwongwan Road on the opposite side of the district — accessible via Bus 134/191 toward MRT Purple Line · Room@Vipa on Vibhavadi side is closest to SRT Bang Khen station (Red Line) at ~750 m, handy for Don Mueang Airport · All seven properties offer free parking for guests who drive.

entries.storyHtml: Livotel Hotel @ Kaset Nawamin Bangkok is a 159-room 3-star on Phahonyothin 34 Soi 11 with the most reviews in the district — 8.6/10 from 1,446 Trip.com guests. That volume of feedback, built up across thousands of genuine stays by university parents, business visitors and Paolo Hospital patients, is the clearest signal of consistent reliability. More than 100 free parking spaces (including coaches) is the headline practical advantage — genuinely hard to find anywhere in Bangkok. BTS Kasetsart University is a 5-minute motorbike-taxi ride away; fitness centre, restaurant and stable Wi-Fi are all on site. Honest note: no pool, some rooms show their age, and a handful of reviews mention insects in bathrooms — the team is reported to fix issues promptly when flagged.
entries.tipHtml: Tip: a motorbike taxi from the hotel entrance to BTS Kasetsart University costs around 15–20 baht and beats walking in Bangkok heat. During graduation season at Kasetsart University, call ahead to confirm parking availability.

entries.storyHtml: Missoniya Hotel is a 42-room 3-star boutique on Ngamwongwan Road, open since 2010, with the highest Cleanliness score in this roundup at 9.6/10. The Japanese minimal design — calm, uncluttered rooms, scented lobby, natural tones — offers a noticeably different atmosphere from typical budget hotels in a university neighbourhood. Buses 134 and 191 stop directly outside, connecting the Ngamwongwan side to the MRT Purple Line and the wider city. Important location note: Missoniya is on Ngamwongwan Road, not the Phahonyothin-BTS corridor. BTS Kasetsart University is roughly 3 km away on the other side of the district and requires Bus 134 or Grab to reach. Critical practical note: parking is extremely limited at 2–3 cars only — if you are driving, call ahead.
entries.tipHtml: Tip: book the King with Deluxe Patio View — the price premium over the standard room is small but the private balcony makes morning coffee a highlight that repeat guests specifically mention. If driving, call the hotel to confirm parking before you set out.

entries.storyHtml: P24 at Kaset is a 26-room boutique aparthotel on Phahonyothin 36 Soi, open since 2016, sitting directly opposite the Kasetsart University Bangkhen gate — Staff score 9.8, Location 9.3, Value 9.0. The Thai loft-industrial design — high ceilings, exposed brick, warm timber — makes it one of the most characterful stays in the district at this price. BTS Sena Nikhom is a 5-minute walk at 400 m. entries.storyHtml: Room@Vipa is a 33-room boutique guesthouse on Vibhavadi Rangsit 44, open since 2014. What separates it from other budget options is not the facilities but the loyalty it has earned: multiple TripAdvisor reviewers describe returning 10–15 times, mentioning that staff remember their name and that it 'feels like home'. SRT Bang Khen station on the Red Line is a 10-minute walk at roughly 750 m — a direct train to Don Mueang Airport makes it a logical base for frequent flyers on a budget. A shared pantry on the third floor (fridge, microwave, toaster), a lift, free parking and a 7-Eleven next door all add practical value. Honest caveats: some beds are on the firm side, the Single room has a shared bathroom, some rooms have sparse furnishings, and the deep soi location makes finding it on a first visit genuinely tricky — share a location pin with the hotel before you travel.
entries.tipHtml: Tip: share your location pin with the hotel via Line before you set out — the soi is deep and the signage from the road is easy to miss. The Red Line train from Bang Khen to Don Mueang Airport is far cheaper than Grab and takes roughly the same time off-peak.

faqTitle: FAQ — Kaset-Nawamin Hotels: Common Traveller Questions

faq.q: Where exactly is the Kaset-Nawamin district and how do I get there?
faq.a: Kaset-Nawamin is in northern Bangkok, covering the area around Kasetsart University Bangkhen, Kaset Junction and Ngamwongwan Road. The BTS Green Line serves the district via three stations: Ratchayothin, Kasetsart University and Sena Nikhom. Guests on the Vibhavadi side can use SRT Bang Khen station (Red Line) for direct trains to Don Mueang Airport and Krung Thep Aphiwat terminal. Bus routes 134 and 191 connect Ngamwongwan Road to the MRT Purple Line.

faq.q: Which hotel in the Kaset area has the highest guest score?
faq.a: Metro Hotel Phahonyothin 35 holds the highest score in this roundup at 9.0/10 from 261 reviews — Service 9.1, Location 9.0, opened 2025, BTS Ratchayothin 5-minute walk, from THB 800/night. That said, Livotel Hotel @ Kaset Nawamin has a much larger sample at 1,446 reviews with a score of 8.6 — arguably a more reliable long-run indicator of consistency.

faq.q: Which hotel is closest to BTS in the Kaset-Nawamin area?
faq.a: Two properties tie for the shortest BTS walk: Metro Hotel Phahonyothin 35 (BTS Ratchayothin, ~400 m, 5-min walk) and P24 at Kaset (BTS Sena Nikhom, ~400 m, 5-min walk). Pannapat Place is 600 m from BTS Ratchayothin (8-min walk). The Maruay Garden Hotel is a 5-minute walk to BTS Kasetsart University.

faq.q: Which hotel in Kaset has the best free parking?
faq.a: Livotel Hotel @ Kaset Nawamin has the most generous free parking — over 100 spaces including coaches, making it the clear choice for guests driving from outside Bangkok. Maruay Garden, Pannapat Place, Metro Hotel Phahonyothin 35 and Room@Vipa also offer free parking, on a smaller scale. Missoniya Hotel has very limited parking — only 2–3 spaces; call ahead if you are driving.

faq.q: How convenient is Kaset-Nawamin for Don Mueang Airport (DMK)?
faq.a: Very convenient. Don Mueang Airport is 9–14 km from the district — roughly 15–25 minutes by Grab or taxi depending on traffic. Room@Vipa on the Vibhavadi side is ~750 m from SRT Bang Khen station, where the Red Line runs directly to Don Mueang. Alternatively, BTS from Kasetsart University connects to the Red Line at Mo Chit/Krung Thep Aphiwat for the same route.

faq.q: Are there good hotels under THB 700 in Kaset-Nawamin?
faq.a: Yes, two options: Room@Vipa starts at THB 550 (Single with shared bathroom) or THB 750 (Twin/Double with private bathroom), score 8.7, Location 9.2, with a loyal repeat-guest community. Missoniya Hotel starts at THB 620, score 8.7, Cleanliness 9.6, Japanese-style boutique on Ngamwongwan Road. Neither has a pool, but both score consistently well for cleanliness and staff friendliness.
